newsitem.title: CHINA: China province '97 andalusite output seen 15,000 T.
newsitem.headline: China province '97 andalusite output seen 15,000 T.

text.p: China's central province of Henan is expected to produce 15,000 tonnes of andalusite in 1997, the International Business Daily said on Friday.
Henan, together with the eastern province of Shandong, had previously maintained annual production of 8,000 tonnes of andalusite, it said. Nearly 70 percent of the output was exported.
Henan alone was expected to turn out 15,000 tonnes in 1997 because of expanding production capacity, the newspaper said. It did not gave a projection of Shandong's output.
Andalusite is a fire-resistant material used in metallurgy, construction materials, chemicals and machinery industries.
"Production capacity in Henan is being expanded," an official of the Ministry of Metallurgical Industry said by telephone.
China has started to build its largest andalusite production base in Henan with annual capacity of 5,000 tonnes after it is completed, he said.
He did not say when the project would be completed, but said production had already started.
Rising demand, especially from the steel industry, was expected to fuel andalusite prices in the next two years, the International Business Daily said, it did not give figures.
"Domestic demand is also strong," the ministry official said.
